clue.text: Stolen food, my delight in Lincolnshire

definitions.text: Stolen food, my delight in Lincolnshire

parts.words: Stolen food, my delight in Lincolnshire
parts.note: food taken illegally from an estate, and a nod to the folk song The Lincolnshire Poacher, whose refrain is 'tis my delight on a shining night'

explanation.surface: A thief in Lincolnshire boasts about the stolen dinner he enjoys.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lincolnshire Poacher is a traditional English folk song whose chorus runs 'Oh, 'tis my delight on a shining night'. A poacher's food is stolen, and the breakfast dish cooked in simmering water carries the same verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The breakfast dish is named for a cooking method that shares its verb with illegal hunting, so it reads as stolen fare.

clue.text: Made by a wolf way over the mountains

definitions.meaning: a wolf is a womaniser, and what he makes at a woman is an amorous advance
a route through a gap in a mountain range, such as an Alpine col

explanation.surface: A wolf leaves its track across the mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both a flirtatious advance (to make one) and a gap or col through high ground.

clue.text: First male worker proves most intransigent

parts.note: Adam is the first man in the Book of Genesis
the ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: The first man and a labourer turn out to be the stubbornest of all.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone utterly unyielding in an opinion refuses to budge, the very height of intransigence.

clue.text: Invalid describes the complaint

parts.note: read 'Invalid' as not valid: the complaint is one where the sufferer's illness is imagined rather than real

explanation.surface: A sick person tells the doctor what is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invalid' looks like a noun for a sick person, but read it as 'in-valid', untrue: the complaint is a baseless one, an imagined illness.
explanation.definitionFit: This disorder is anxious belief in illnesses one does not have, so the invalid's complaint is not valid.

clue.text: Bishop could be a second one

indicators.note: says the letters that follow might be rearranged into something else

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A bishop might be the second one in line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges ASECOND plus I (one).
explanation.definitionFit: A diocesan is the bishop who presides over a diocese, as distinct from a suffragan.

clue.text: One in the Zoology group is a brilliant fellow

indicators.note: the word 'in' puts the numeral inside the classification group

parts.note: a genus is a group in biological classification, between family and species
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone in the zoology department is a brilliant fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I inside GENUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of exceptional intellect or talent is a prodigy of the brilliant kind.

clue.text: US prison ship

definitions.meaning: in American usage a lock-up, especially a naval one aboard ship

explanation.surface: An American jail aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a naval guardroom in American slang and a two-masted sailing vessel.

clue.text: Cooked an hour, nothing less, horse makes tasty stew

indicators.note: cooking mixes things up, so the letters are rearranged
the word 'less' takes the following piece out of the hour

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O
a barb is a Barbary horse, a breed from North Africa

explanation.surface: An hour's cooking and a horse produce a tasty stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' removes the O (nothing) from the hour before 'Cooked' rearranges what is left; a barb is a horse of the Barbary breed from North Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The pink stalks are usually stewed with sugar, so the plant makes a tasty stewed dessert.

clue.text: Pop a hot-stuff existentialist'?

parts.note: ginger is a hot spice
read as 'one who is': a be-er, one who exists

explanation.surface: A fiery philosopher who is something of a pop star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'existentialist' is taken literally as one who exists, a 'be-er'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop is a fizzy soft drink, and this spiced fizzy brew is one.

clue.text: It shows how frothy-headed people can be

definitions.text: It shows how frothy-headed people can be

parts.words: It shows how frothy-headed people can be
parts.note: frothy-headed seems to mean empty-headed, but a head lathered with suds during a hair wash is literally frothy

explanation.surface: A remark on how silly some airheads are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frothy-headed' looks like an insult meaning frivolous; it is literal, a head covered in lather.
explanation.definitionFit: Washing hair with soapy lather leaves a person with a head full of foam.

clue.text: Not quite done-what he did with ladies' hearts!

definitions.text: Not quite done-what he did with ladies' hearts!

parts.words: Not quite done-what he did with ladies' hearts!
parts.note: the legendary seducer Don ... without his title Don, 'done', leaves the name, which sounds like 'won', what he did to women's hearts

explanation.surface: A rake leaves the job unfinished, having won the hearts of ladies.
explanation.walkthrough: The famous seducer is Don Juan; drop 'Don' (heard as 'done') and what remains is his first name, which in English mouths sounds like 'won'.
explanation.definitionFit: Don Juan is the libertine of Spanish legend who conquered women's affections, so his name is what remains.

clue.text: Less than intimate knowledge

parts.note: familiarity with a person or subject that falls short of close friendship or deep expertise

explanation.surface: Knowing something only slightly.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowing someone casually, short of friendship, is a slight familiarity rather than closeness.

clue.text: Stuff it back.1 Have some brandy

indicators.note: the word 'back' turns the synonym for stuff the other way round

parts.note: to stuff is to cram

explanation.surface: Told to shove it, someone pours a drink instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses CRAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc is a spirit distilled from grape pressings left after winemaking.

clue.text: Proclaim the composing of a -.nice tune

indicators.note: composing arranges notes, so the letters of the following words are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A composer announces a nice new tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the composing of' rearranges ANICETUNE.
explanation.definitionFit: To say something out loud clearly, or state it publicly, is to declare it.

clue.text: The vicar's duty

parts.note: the office held by a parish priest, who is the holder of a church living

explanation.surface: What a parson must do.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicar holds a benefice, and the holding of that office is its tenure.

clue.text: Grand sporting event for a man of the people

definitions.meaning: the Grand ... is Britain's most famous steeplechase horse race, run at Aintree
a citizen of a particular country

explanation.surface: A big race for the common man.
explanation.walkthrough: The Grand National is a famous British horse race over fences, run each spring at Aintree near Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names both the famous steeplechase (with Grand) and a citizen of a given country.

clue.text: Riot of Universal Boys' Brigade in revolutionary centre .

indicators.note: the word 'in' places the two abbreviations inside the centre

parts.note: a hub is the centre of a revolving wheel
U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal
BB is the abbreviation for the Boys' Brigade, a Christian youth organisation

explanation.surface: Youth group members cause chaos in a centre of revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' suggests a reversal or rebels, but it describes the hub, the part a wheel turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy tumult or din is an uproar of the kind a riot makes.

clue.text: Are varieties of oil needed in an aircraft's wing?

indicators.note: varieties are different versions, so the letters take a different form

explanation.surface: Does an aircraft's wing need different grades of oil?
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a question about lubricants, but 'varieties' rearranges only ARE, and the next two words are taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: A wing is shaped in cross-section to give lift, and that lifting surface is its technical name.

clue.text: Is nudity so disorderly ?

indicators.note: something disorderly is out of order, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Asking whether going naked counts as unruly behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorderly' rearranges NUDITY; the whole clue doubles as the definition, since nakedness leaves clothes strewn about.
explanation.definitionFit: Being messy or not neat is being disorderly.

clue.text: Trade Union's blow, or clump

parts.note: TU is the abbreviation for trade union, with the possessive S
a sock is a punch

explanation.surface: A union's punch, or a cluster of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A tussock is a dense tuft of grass, a clump growing together.

clue.text: Company has same backing, note not very good

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the two pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: idem is Latin for the same, used in references
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A firm with the same support and a memo, not very impressive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses CO plus IDEM together, giving MEDIOC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of only middling quality, ordinary and unremarkable, is not very good.

clue.text: French horn thus has a Napoleonic origin

parts.note: cor is French for horn
sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quoted error

explanation.surface: A French horn player traces its origins back to Napoleon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French horn' looks like the instrument, but it asks for the French word for horn.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon Bonaparte was born on this island, so it is where the emperor came from.

clue.text: False report of French batting failure?

definitions.meaning: an unfounded rumour or hoax story
the French word for duck, and a duck in cricket is a score of nought

explanation.surface: A rumour about a French batsman's poor innings.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman out without scoring makes a 'duck'; canard is the French for duck.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is French for a duck, which in cricket is a score of nothing, and in English means a hoax or rumour.

clue.text: Graduates fuss about money — their sole affliction ?

indicators.note: about here means next to, so the fuss is placed alongside the money

parts.note: BAs are Bachelors of Arts
tin is old slang for cash
ado is fuss or bother

explanation.surface: University graduates make a fuss about money, their only problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sole' looks like 'only' but means the sole of the foot: the punishment beats the soles.
explanation.definitionFit: Bastinado is a punishment of caning the soles of the feet, so it afflicts the sole.

clue.text: Chuck out of the racing game

definitions.meaning: horse racing as a sport and business

explanation.surface: Being thrown out of horse racing.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb (with 'out') means to eject, and the noun names horse racing, run on grass tracks.

clue.text: " Wreathed Smiles. Such as hang on - --'s cheek " (Milton)

definitions.text: " Wreathed Smiles. Such as hang on - --'s cheek " (Milton)

parts.words: " Wreathed Smiles. Such as hang on - --'s cheek " (Milton)
parts.note: a line from Milton's poem L'Allegro, with the name of the cupbearer goddess of youth left blank

explanation.surface: A fill-in-the-blank quotation from Milton's poem about mirth.
explanation.walkthrough: Milton's L'Allegro lists 'Nods, and Becks, and Wreathed Smiles, Such as hang on —'s cheek'; the blank is the Greek goddess of youth, daughter of Zeus and Hera.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek goddess of youth and cupbearer to the gods is the one whose cheek Milton gives smiles.

clue.text: Sort of light pole one's redesigned

parts.note: N is the north pole

indicators.note: something redesigned is given a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word one, with 's as a link

explanation.surface: A lamp-post is redesigned with a new sort of light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redesigned' turns ONE into EON; 'pole' is a compass pole, not a post.
explanation.definitionFit: This gas glows red in discharge tubes and gives its name to bright advertising signs.

clue.text: Dressing for the county in Ireland? Insane arrangement

parts.note: Mayo is a county in the west of Ireland

indicators.note: an arrangement puts the letters of the preceding word into a new order

explanation.surface: Something to wear for an Irish county, an arrangement that seems mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressing' suggests clothing; it is a salad dressing. 'arrangement' rearranges INSANE.
explanation.definitionFit: This emulsion of egg yolk and oil is a sauce dressed over salads.

clue.text: Slavery's all right in the old environment

indicators.note: environment means surroundings, so the old article surrounds the other piece

parts.note: ye is an old spelling of the
OK means all right

explanation.surface: Slavery was acceptable in the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Slavery's' stands for 'is'. Ye is the old form of 'the', its Y originally the letter thorn; 'environment' wraps it round the other piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Bondage or servitude is the burden of a harness, figuratively a yoke laid on the enslaved.

clue.text: Corrupt man was Roman egghead

parts.note: a grown man is an adult
erat is Latin for 'was', the Romans' word
read as egg's head, the first letter of egg

explanation.surface: A man who was a Roman intellectual turns corrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' looks like an intellectual; read it as the head of 'egg', its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To corrupt something is to make it impure by adding inferior substances, so the verbs match.
